views.name: classes_with_room_and_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Classes.ClassID,
  Classes.SubjectID,
  Classes.ClassRoomID,
  Classes.Credits,
  Classes.StartDate,
  Classes.StartTime,
  Classes.Duration,
  Classes.MondaySchedule,
  Classes.TuesdaySchedule,
  Classes.WednesdaySchedule,
  Classes.ThursdaySchedule,
  Classes.FridaySchedule,
  Classes.SaturdaySchedule,
  Class_Rooms.BuildingCode,
  Class_Rooms.PhoneAvailable,
  Buildings.BuildingName,
  Buildings.NumberOfFloors,
  Buildings.ElevatorAccess,
  Buildings.SiteParkingAvailable
FROM Classes
LEFT JOIN Class_Rooms ON Classes.ClassRoomID = Class_Rooms.ClassRoomID
LEFT JOIN Buildings ON Class_Rooms.BuildingCode = Buildings.BuildingCode

params.description: Provides one-row-per-class details combining class scheduling, assigned classroom, and building attributes.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve class-level schedule and location details (e.g., what room and building a class meets in and on which weekdays). | Filter or report classes by building attributes (e.g., classes in buildings with elevator access or site parking). | Compose timetables that need classroom phone availability or building metadata alongside class schedule fields. | Join class-level information to other one-row-per-class datasets (e.g., enrollments aggregated to class) without duplicating class measures.
params.output_schema: ClassID: unique identifier for the class (derived from Classes.ClassID). | SubjectID: subject reference for the class (derived from Classes.SubjectID). | ClassRoomID: classroom identifier assigned to the class (derived from Classes.ClassRoomID). | Credits: credit value for the class (derived from Classes.Credits). | StartDate: class start date (derived from Classes.StartDate). | StartTime: class start time (derived from Classes.StartTime). | Duration: class duration (derived from Classes.Duration). | MondaySchedule: flag/indicator that the class meets on Monday (derived from Classes.MondaySchedule). | TuesdaySchedule: flag/indicator that the class meets on Tuesday (derived from Classes.TuesdaySchedule). | WednesdaySchedule: flag/indicator that the class meets on Wednesday (derived from Classes.WednesdaySchedule). | ThursdaySchedule: flag/indicator that the class meets on Thursday (derived from Classes.ThursdaySchedule). | FridaySchedule: flag/indicator that the class meets on Friday (derived from Classes.FridaySchedule). | SaturdaySchedule: flag/indicator that the class meets on Saturday (derived from Classes.SaturdaySchedule). | BuildingCode: building identifier where the classroom is located (derived from Class_Rooms.BuildingCode). | PhoneAvailable: whether the classroom has a phone (derived from Class_Rooms.PhoneAvailable). | BuildingName: human-readable building name (derived from Buildings.BuildingName). | NumberOfFloors: number of floors in the building (derived from Buildings.NumberOfFloors). | ElevatorAccess: whether the building has elevator access (derived from Buildings.ElevatorAccess). | SiteParkingAvailable: whether site parking is available at the building (derived from Buildings.SiteParkingAvailable).
params.grounded_columns: Classes.ClassID | Classes.SubjectID | Classes.ClassRoomID | Classes.Credits | Classes.StartDate | Classes.StartTime | Classes.Duration | Classes.MondaySchedule | Classes.TuesdaySchedule | Classes.WednesdaySchedule | Classes.ThursdaySchedule | Classes.FridaySchedule | Classes.SaturdaySchedule | Class_Rooms.ClassRoomID | Class_Rooms.BuildingCode | Class_Rooms.PhoneAvailable | Buildings.BuildingCode | Buildings.BuildingName | Buildings.NumberOfFloors | Buildings.ElevatorAccess | Buildings.SiteParkingAvailable
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any dimension or view that is one-row-per-class (key = ClassID) on classes.ClassID — safe because this view is one row per ClassID (grain = ClassID) and such joins will not duplicate class-level rows or measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a classroom dimension or view that is one-row-per-ClassRoomID on ClassRoomID — safe because ClassRoomID in this view is at most one row per class; joining to one-row-per-ClassRoomID will not multiply rows for a given class. | do NOT directly join this view to tables or views that are one-to-many from ClassID (for example: student enrollments, meeting occurrences, instructor-assignments that allow multiple rows per ClassID) without first aggregating or deduplicating those tables to one row per ClassID. Such joins would multiply class rows and therefore duplicate any class-level attributes. | do NOT directly join to one-to-many tables keyed to ClassRoomID or BuildingCode (for example: room maintenance logs, building events) without aggregation on that table to the ClassRoomID or BuildingCode level; otherwise building or room-level rows will multiply class rows. | If you need counts or sums from one-to-many related tables (e.g., number of enrolled students, number of instructors), compute those as aggregates grouped by ClassID (or ClassRoomID/BuildingCode as appropriate) before joining to this view to preserve correct cardinality. | Safe composition examples: join to "student_enrollments_with_status" aggregated to ClassID (summed enrollment_count per ClassID), or join to "faculty_full_profile" if that view is one-row-per-faculty and joined via an already-aggregated class->faculty link; unsafe without aggregation: joining this view directly to student_enrollments_with_status if that view contains multiple rows per ClassID will multiply rows.

views.description: Denormalized one-row-per-class offering with classroom and building attributes. Useful when analyzing where classes are held, room facilities, or joining to faculty/students by ClassID. | Use for: List classes with room/building info; Which buildings host the most classes; Find classes in rooms without phone or without elevator access; Join to Faculty_Classes or Student_Schedules for attendance/roster-level queries

views.name: class_schedule_weekday_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ClassID,
  SubjectID,
  ClassRoomID,
  Credits,
  StartDate,
  StartTime,
  Duration,
  MondaySchedule,
  TuesdaySchedule,
  WednesdaySchedule,
  ThursdaySchedule,
  FridaySchedule,
  SaturdaySchedule,
  (CASE WHEN MondaySchedule = 1 THEN 'Mon' ELSE '' END) ||
  (CASE WHEN TuesdaySchedule = 1 THEN (CASE WHEN MondaySchedule = 1 THEN ',' ELSE '' END) || 'Tue' ELSE '' END) ||
  (CASE WHEN WednesdaySchedule = 1 THEN (CASE WHEN MondaySchedule = 1 OR TuesdaySchedule = 1 THEN ',' ELSE '' END) || 'Wed' ELSE '' END) ||
  (CASE WHEN ThursdaySchedule = 1 THEN (CASE WHEN MondaySchedule = 1 OR TuesdaySchedule = 1 OR WednesdaySchedule = 1 THEN ',' ELSE '' END) || 'Thu' ELSE '' END) ||
  (CASE WHEN FridaySchedule = 1 THEN (CASE WHEN MondaySchedule = 1 OR TuesdaySchedule = 1 OR WednesdaySchedule = 1 OR ThursdaySchedule = 1 THEN ',' ELSE '' END) || 'Fri' ELSE '' END) ||
  (CASE WHEN SaturdaySchedule = 1 THEN (CASE WHEN MondaySchedule = 1 OR TuesdaySchedule = 1 OR WednesdaySchedule = 1 OR ThursdaySchedule = 1 OR FridaySchedule = 1 THEN ',' ELSE '' END) || 'Sat' ELSE '' END) AS scheduled_weekdays
FROM Classes

params.description: Provides one-row-per-ClassID weekday schedule flags and a human-readable comma-separated scheduled_weekdays string for each class.
params.when_to_use: List classes and which weekdays they meet (e.g., show all classes that meet on Monday or on Mon/Wed/Fri). | Filter or group classes by meeting days to build timetables or weekly views. | Compose class-level schedules into larger reports (join to subjects, rooms, buildings, instructors) while preserving one-row-per-class granularity. | Create display labels for class meeting days (scheduled_weekdays) for UI or export.
params.output_schema: ClassID: unique identifier for the class (derived from Classes.ClassID). | SubjectID: identifier for the subject this class covers (derived from Classes.SubjectID). | ClassRoomID: identifier for the classroom assigned to the class (derived from Classes.ClassRoomID). | Credits: credit value of the class (derived from Classes.Credits). | StartDate: class start date (derived from Classes.StartDate). | StartTime: class start time (derived from Classes.StartTime). | Duration: class duration (derived from Classes.Duration). | MondaySchedule: integer flag (1/0) indicating the class meets on Monday (derived from Classes.MondaySchedule). | TuesdaySchedule: integer flag (1/0) indicating the class meets on Tuesday (derived from Classes.TuesdaySchedule). | WednesdaySchedule: integer flag (1/0) indicating the class meets on Wednesday (derived from Classes.WednesdaySchedule). | ThursdaySchedule: integer flag (1/0) indicating the class meets on Thursday (derived from Classes.ThursdaySchedule). | FridaySchedule: integer flag (1/0) indicating the class meets on Friday (derived from Classes.FridaySchedule). | SaturdaySchedule: integer flag (1/0) indicating the class meets on Saturday (derived from Classes.SaturdaySchedule). | scheduled_weekdays: text label built by concatenating weekday abbreviations in order (Mon,Tue,Wed,Thu,Fri,Sat) for which the corresponding Schedule flag = 1 (expression built from the weekday flag columns).
params.grounded_columns: Classes.ClassID | Classes.SubjectID | Classes.ClassRoomID | Classes.Credits | Classes.StartDate | Classes.StartTime | Classes.Duration | Classes.MondaySchedule | Classes.TuesdaySchedule | Classes.WednesdaySchedule | Classes.ThursdaySchedule | Classes.FridaySchedule | Classes.SaturdaySchedule
params.metric: scheduled_weekdays = (CASE WHEN Classes.MondaySchedule = 1 THEN 'Mon' ELSE '' END) || (CASE WHEN Classes.TuesdaySchedule = 1 THEN (CASE WHEN Classes.MondaySchedule = 1 THEN ',' ELSE '' END) || 'Tue' ELSE '' END) || (CASE WHEN Classes.WednesdaySchedule = 1 THEN (CASE WHEN Classes.MondaySchedule = 1 OR Classes.TuesdaySchedule = 1 THEN ',' ELSE '' END) || 'Wed' ELSE '' END) || (CASE WHEN Classes.ThursdaySchedule = 1 THEN (CASE WHEN Classes.MondaySchedule = 1 OR Classes.TuesdaySchedule = 1 OR Classes.WednesdaySchedule = 1 THEN ',' ELSE '' END) || 'Thu' ELSE '' END) || (CASE WHEN Classes.FridaySchedule = 1 THEN (CASE WHEN Classes.MondaySchedule = 1 OR Classes.TuesdaySchedule = 1 OR Classes.WednesdaySchedule = 1 OR Classes.ThursdaySchedule = 1 THEN ',' ELSE '' END) || 'Fri' ELSE '' END) || (CASE WHEN Classes.SaturdaySchedule = 1 THEN (CASE WHEN Classes.MondaySchedule = 1 OR Classes.TuesdaySchedule = 1 OR Classes.WednesdaySchedule = 1 OR Classes.ThursdaySchedule = 1 OR Classes.FridaySchedule = 1 THEN ',' ELSE '' END) || 'Sat' ELSE '' END)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to subject or room dimension views/tables on SubjectID or ClassRoomID respectively — safe because this view has one row per Classes.ClassID and Subject/Room tables are expected to be one-row-per-SubjectID or one-row-per-ClassRoomID, so joining on SubjectID or ClassRoomID will not duplicate this view's rows (e.g., JOIN subject_category_with_department ON class_schedule_weekday_flags.SubjectID = subject_category_with_department.SubjectID). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to students_with_major_and_gpa or faculty_full_profile (one-row-per-entity) on their respective keys only if those tables are one-row-per-key (e.g., instructor assignments must be one-row-per-class to avoid duplication). | do NOT blindly join to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., student_enrollments_with_status, faculty_subject_proficiency, faculty_teaching_load) without first aggregating those child rows to class-level, because those views contain multiple rows per ClassID or SubjectID and would multiply this view's rows/measures. Instead: aggregate enrollments or loads to ClassID (or SubjectID) first, e.g., SELECT ClassID, COUNT(*) AS enrolled_count FROM student_enrollments_with_status GROUP BY ClassID, then join that result to class_schedule_weekday_flags on ClassID. | if composing with sibling JOIN views that themselves expand rows (marked JOIN), verify they are one-row-per-key before joining; if not, re-aggregate or use DISTINCT ON keys to preserve class-level cardinality. | summary: safe to join on keys that are one-to-one with Classes.ClassID/SubjectID/ClassRoomID; avoid direct joins to known one-to-many views (enrollments, proficiency, teaching_load) without reduction to one row per ClassID/SubjectID.

views.description: Normalized weekly schedule flags per class with a derived descriptive column listing scheduled weekdays. Useful for filtering or grouping classes by meeting days or computing daily loads. | Use for: Find classes meeting on a particular weekday; Aggregate class counts by weekday; Filter classes that meet multiple specific weekdays

views.name: faculty_full_profile
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Staff.StaffID,
  Staff.StfFirstName,
  Staff.StfLastname,
  Staff.StfStreetAddress,
  Staff.StfCity,
  Staff.StfState,
  Staff.StfZipCode,
  Staff.StfAreaCode,
  Staff.StfPhoneNumber,
  Staff.Salary,
  Staff.DateHired,
  Staff.Position,
  Faculty.Title,
  Faculty.Status,
  Faculty.Tenured,
  Departments.DepartmentID AS DepartmentID,
  Departments.DeptName AS DeptName,
  Departments.DeptChair AS DeptChair
FROM Staff
LEFT JOIN Faculty ON Staff.StaffID = Faculty.StaffID
LEFT JOIN Departments ON Staff.StaffID = Departments.DeptChair

params.description: Provides one-row-per-staff member combining Staff demographic/pay/hire info with optional faculty attributes and the department (if the staff is a department chair).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve a faculty member or staff member full profile (name, contact, salary, hire date) possibly enriched with faculty status, title, and tenure. | Report lists of faculty/staff with their department when the staff person is a department chair. | Compose higher-level reports that need a single-row representation of a staff person so additional aggregations (counts, sums) can be built safely on top. | Filter or join on StaffID to bring profile attributes into other queries (e.g., combine with teaching load, class assignments, or proficiency) while preserving one-row-per-staff semantics.
params.output_schema: StaffID: unique staff identifier — derived from Staff.StaffID | StfFirstName: staff first name — derived from Staff.StfFirstName | StfLastname: staff last name — derived from Staff.StfLastname | StfStreetAddress: street address of staff — derived from Staff.StfStreetAddress | StfCity: city of staff — derived from Staff.StfCity | StfState: state of staff — derived from Staff.StfState | StfZipCode: zip code of staff — derived from Staff.StfZipCode | StfAreaCode: phone area code of staff — derived from Staff.StfAreaCode | StfPhoneNumber: phone number of staff — derived from Staff.StfPhoneNumber | Salary: staff salary (base pay) — derived from Staff.Salary | DateHired: date staff was hired — derived from Staff.DateHired | Position: staff position/job title (HR) — derived from Staff.Position | Title: faculty title/appointment (e.g., Professor) — derived from Faculty.Title | Status: faculty status (e.g., Active/Inactive) — derived from Faculty.Status | Tenured: tenure flag or status for faculty — derived from Faculty.Tenured | DepartmentID: department identifier when this staff is recorded as DeptChair — derived from Departments.DepartmentID | DeptName: department name when this staff is recorded as DeptChair — derived from Departments.DeptName | DeptChair: department chair StaffID for the department row joined (equals Staff.StaffID when present) — derived from Departments.DeptChair
params.grounded_columns: Staff.StaffID | Staff.StfFirstName | Staff.StfLastname | Staff.StfStreetAddress | Staff.StfCity | Staff.StfState | Staff.StfZipCode | Staff.StfAreaCode | Staff.StfPhoneNumber | Staff.Salary | Staff.DateHired | Staff.Position | Faculty.StaffID | Faculty.Title | Faculty.Status | Faculty.Tenured | Departments.DepartmentID | Departments.DeptName | Departments.DeptChair
params.metric: There are no aggregated metrics computed in this view; all outputs are direct column projections (no SUM/COUNT/AVG expressions).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to Staff dimension or any one-row-per-StaffID view on StaffID — safe because this view is one-row-per Staff.StaffID (the FROM is Staff and no aggregation is performed). Example: join faculty_full_profile to faculty_teaching_load on StaffID (one-row-per-staff teaching-load aggregate) — safe because the teaching-load view should be one-row-per-StaffID, so measures won't be multiplied. | safe to join on StaffID to sibling one-row-per-StaffID views such as top_faculty_by_proficiency_rank (if that view is one-row-per-StaffID) — the planner must ensure the sibling is also one-row-per-StaffID to avoid duplication. | do NOT directly join this view to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., classes_with_room_and_building, class_schedule_weekday_flags, student_enrollments_with_status, faculty_subject_proficiency, students_with_major_and_gpa) without first aggregating or deduplicating the many-side by StaffID — joining to those many-side tables will multiply rows and thereby duplicate any measures that might be aggregated later. For example, joining faculty_full_profile to classes_with_room_and_building on StaffID (if classes are many per staff) will produce one output row per class per staff and thus is NOT cardinality-safe for metrics like Salary unless you re-aggregate (e.g., sum or avg) after the join or pre-aggregate classes to one row per StaffID. | when you need counts or sums of related many-side entities (e.g., number of classes taught, number of subjects proficient), perform the aggregation on the many-side first (produce one-row-per-StaffID aggregates) and then join those aggregated results to faculty_full_profile on StaffID — this preserves correct metric semantics. | because Departments is LEFT JOINed on Departments.DeptChair = Staff.StaffID, DepartmentID/DeptName/DeptChair will only be non-null when the staff member is a department chair. Do not assume that DeptName implies primary department assignment for general faculty membership; there is no base-column linking Faculty to Departments by Faculty membership in this view.

views.description: One row per faculty person combining Staff and Faculty attributes and department chair status. Useful for analyses of faculty salaries, tenure, and contact details. | Use for: List faculty with salary and tenure info; Find department chairs and their contact/salary details; Join faculty to Faculty_Classes or Faculty_Subjects for teaching/proficiency analyses

views.name: faculty_subject_proficiency
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  SubjectID,
  COUNT(StaffID) AS faculty_count,
  AVG(ProficiencyRating) AS avg_ProficiencyRating,
  MIN(ProficiencyRating) AS min_ProficiencyRating,
  MAX(ProficiencyRating) AS max_ProficiencyRating
FROM Faculty_Subjects
GROUP BY SubjectID

params.description: Per-subject aggregation of faculty counts and summary statistics (avg/min/max) of faculty proficiency ratings for that subject.
params.when_to_use: Report total number of faculty associated with each subject | Compare average, minimum, or maximum faculty proficiency by subject | Filter or rank subjects by faculty_count or avg_ProficiencyRating | Compose into larger reports that need one-row-per-subject faculty proficiency metrics (e.g., join subject-level attributes or departments)
params.output_schema: SubjectID: identifier for the subject; derives directly from Faculty_Subjects.SubjectID (GROUP BY key) | faculty_count: number of faculty rows associated with the subject; derives from COUNT(StaffID) over Faculty_Subjects | avg_ProficiencyRating: average of ProficiencyRating values for faculty tied to the subject; derives from AVG(ProficiencyRating) over Faculty_Subjects | min_ProficiencyRating: minimum ProficiencyRating among faculty for the subject; derives from MIN(ProficiencyRating) over Faculty_Subjects | max_ProficiencyRating: maximum ProficiencyRating among faculty for the subject; derives from MAX(ProficiencyRating) over Faculty_Subjects
params.metric: faculty_count = COUNT(Faculty_Subjects.StaffID) | avg_ProficiencyRating = AVG(Faculty_Subjects.ProficiencyRating) | min_ProficiencyRating = MIN(Faculty_Subjects.ProficiencyRating) | max_ProficiencyRating = MAX(Faculty_Subjects.ProficiencyRating)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to subject_category_with_department on SubjectID — safe because this view is one-row-per-SubjectID, so joining to a one-row-per-SubjectID dimension (subject_category_with_department) will NOT duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to top_faculty_by_proficiency_rank on SubjectID only when top_faculty_by_proficiency_rank is also one-row-per-SubjectID (e.g., ranked top faculty aggregated to SubjectID); safe if the sibling view is aggregated to SubjectID. | do NOT join directly to Faculty_Subjects (the base table) or any other one-to-many table keyed by SubjectID (for example, faculty_full_profile if it contains multiple rows per StaffID or multiple subject associations) without re-aggregation — doing so will multiply faculty_count and distort avg/min/max unless you re-aggregate after the join. | do NOT join to one-to-many result sets such as faculty_teaching_load (if it is one row per class taught) or class_schedule_weekday_flags (if expanded per class/weekday) on SubjectID without first reducing those tables to one row per SubjectID or otherwise adjusting aggregation; otherwise the measures in this view will be duplicated. | If you need subject-level metrics combined with row-level details (e.g., list of faculty), join this view to the detail table on SubjectID but treat the aggregated metrics as stable per-subject lookups (use them only at subject grain) or re-aggregate after the join to restore correct measures. | When composing further aggregations: this view is already at the grain SubjectID. To compute higher-level aggregates (e.g., department-level average of avg_ProficiencyRating), use weighted-aware logic if you need true aggregated averages (e.g., compute department_avg = SUM(avg_ProficiencyRating * faculty_count) / SUM(faculty_count)) because simple AVG(avg_ProficiencyRating) would treat subjects equally rather than weighting by faculty_count.

views.description: Aggregated proficiency metrics per subject: average, min, max ProficiencyRating and count of faculty with a rating. Useful for measuring subject coverage and identifying subjects with few instructors. | Use for: Which subjects have the most/least faculty proficiency; Average proficiency rating by subject; Identify subjects lacking proficient instructors

views.name: student_enrollments_with_status
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Student_Schedules.StudentID,
  Student_Schedules.ClassID,
  Student_Schedules.ClassStatus,
  Student_Schedules.Grade,
  Student_Class_Status.ClassStatusDescription,
  Students.StudFirstName,
  Students.StudLastName,
  Students.StudMajor,
  Students.StudGPA
FROM Student_Schedules
LEFT JOIN Student_Class_Status ON Student_Schedules.ClassStatus = Student_Class_Status.ClassStatus
LEFT JOIN Students ON Student_Schedules.StudentID = Students.StudentID

params.description: Provides one row per student enrollment in a class, combining enrollment status, grade, and basic student profile fields to answer questions about who is enrolled in which class and their status/grade.
params.when_to_use: List enrollments for a given class, student, or set of classes (e.g., who is enrolled in ClassID = X and what is their status/grade). | Filter or group enrollments by ClassStatus (e.g., active, dropped) and return student identifying/profile attributes. | Join enrollment-level data to class- or schedule-level details when building class rosters, attendance or grade reports (use cardinality-safe joins as described). | Serve as the enrollment-detail input for downstream aggregations (e.g., counts of enrolled students by status, average grade per class) — but re-aggregate at the desired grain rather than relying on this view to aggregate.
params.output_schema: StudentID: identifier of the student for this enrollment — derived from Student_Schedules.StudentID | ClassID: identifier of the class for this enrollment — derived from Student_Schedules.ClassID | ClassStatus: enrollment status code for this student-class row (e.g., enrolled, dropped) — derived from Student_Schedules.ClassStatus | Grade: grade awarded/recorded for this student in this class (may be NULL) — derived from Student_Schedules.Grade | ClassStatusDescription: human-readable description of the ClassStatus code — derived from Student_Class_Status.ClassStatusDescription (joined on Student_Schedules.ClassStatus = Student_Class_Status.ClassStatus) | StudFirstName: student's first name — derived from Students.StudFirstName (joined on Student_Schedules.StudentID = Students.StudentID) | StudLastName: student's last name — derived from Students.StudLastName | StudMajor: student's declared major — derived from Students.StudMajor | StudGPA: student's GPA at the Students table level — derived from Students.StudGPA
params.grounded_columns: Student_Schedules.StudentID | Student_Schedules.ClassID | Student_Schedules.ClassStatus | Student_Schedules.Grade | Student_Class_Status.ClassStatus | Student_Class_Status.ClassStatusDescription | Students.StudentID | Students.StudFirstName | Students.StudLastName | Students.StudMajor | Students.StudGPA
params.metric: This view has no aggregated metrics at its grain; all columns are direct projections or lookups. If you derive metrics from this view, compute them by re-aggregation at the desired grain. Example safe derived metrics (computed externally): | enrolled_count = COUNT(*) -- count of rows in this view grouped by ClassID (or StudentID) representing number of enrollments | avg_grade = AVG(Grade) -- average of Grade over this view after filtering to desired ClassID or ClassStatus (NULLs handled per SQL dialect) | pct_active = SUM(CASE WHEN ClassStatus = <active_code> THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) -- proportion active by group
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE: join to classes_with_room_and_building on ClassID — safe because classes_with_room_and_building is one-row-per-ClassID (class dimension). Joining will not multiply enrollment rows if the class view is at ClassID grain. | Cardinality-SAFE: join to subject_category_with_department on ClassID -> (if that view exposes ClassID as a primary key/class grain) — only safe when the target view/table is one-row-per-ClassID; verify the sibling view's grain before joining. | Cardinality-SAFE: join to students_with_major_and_gpa on StudentID — safe because that view is a student-level (one-row-per-StudentID) normalization of Students; joining will attach student attributes without duplicating enrollment rows. | UNSAFE WITHOUT RE-AGGREGATION: do NOT join this view to any one-to-many detail (e.g., a per-week attendance table, multiple meeting times, or any schedule detail that has multiple rows per StudentID+ClassID) without first aggregating the detail to the enrollment grain (StudentID, ClassID). Such joins would multiply rows and thus duplicate counts/metrics derived from this view. | UNSAFE WITHOUT RE-AGGREGATION: do NOT join directly to faculty_teaching_load, faculty_subject_proficiency, or faculty_full_profile unless you join via a class->faculty mapping that is one-to-one per ClassID. If those sibling views are multi-row per ClassID (e.g., per-term or per-subject rows), aggregate or restrict them to one row per ClassID before joining to avoid duplicating enrollments. | Guideline for planners: when composing aggregates that count enrollments or compute averages from this view, perform the aggregation after all joins, or ensure any joined table is reduced to one row per the join key(s) (StudentID or ClassID) via GROUP BY or by selecting a deduplicated dimension keyed to the same grain (StudentID or ClassID).

views.description: One row per student-class enrollment with class status description and student basic info. Useful for grade/reporting, enrollment counts, and status-based cohorts (e.g., completed vs enrolled). | Use for: List student grades with human-readable status; Count enrolled vs completed by class; Join to Classes or Subjects for performance by course

views.name: subject_category_with_department
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Subjects.SubjectID,
  Subjects.CategoryID,
  Subjects.SubjectCode,
  Subjects.SubjectName,
  Subjects.SubjectPreReq,
  Subjects.SubjectDescription,
  Categories.CategoryDescription,
  Categories.DepartmentID
FROM Subjects
LEFT JOIN Categories ON Subjects.CategoryID = Categories.CategoryID

params.description: Provides subject (course) details along with their category description and owning department; one row per SubjectID.
params.when_to_use: Look up full subject metadata (code, name, prereqs, description) optionally with category and department context. | Filter or list subjects by CategoryID or DepartmentID. | Use as a base to join enrollment, class, or faculty assignments when you need subject-level attributes. | Compose subject-level reports (counts, flags) where each SubjectID should be represented once.
params.output_schema: SubjectID: unique identifier for the subject (derived from Subjects.SubjectID) | CategoryID: identifier for the category this subject belongs to (derived from Subjects.CategoryID) | SubjectCode: short code for the subject (derived from Subjects.SubjectCode) | SubjectName: human-readable name of the subject (derived from Subjects.SubjectName) | SubjectPreReq: prerequisite information for the subject (derived from Subjects.SubjectPreReq) | SubjectDescription: detailed description of the subject (derived from Subjects.SubjectDescription) | CategoryDescription: human-readable description of the category (derived from Categories.CategoryDescription) | DepartmentID: identifier for the department that owns the category (derived from Categories.DepartmentID)
params.grounded_columns: Subjects.SubjectID | Subjects.CategoryID | Subjects.SubjectCode | Subjects.SubjectName | Subjects.SubjectPreReq | Subjects.SubjectDescription | Categories.CategoryDescription | Categories.DepartmentID | Categories.CategoryID
params.metric: row_count_subject = COUNT(DISTINCT Subjects.SubjectID) -- implicit grain metric: one row per SubjectID | subject_exists_flag = CASE WHEN Subjects.SubjectID IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END -- existence indicator at the SubjectID grain
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensions that are one-to-one with SubjectID without re-aggregation — e.g., join to a subjects-details dimension on SubjectID — safe because this view is one-row-per-SubjectID so such joins do NOT duplicate rows. | Safe to join to faculty_subject_proficiency (AGG) on SubjectID only if faculty_subject_proficiency is pre-aggregated to one row per SubjectID (otherwise aggregate faculty_subject_proficiency to SubjectID first). | Safe to join to student_enrollments_with_status (JOIN) only when you intend to expand subject rows into multiple enrollment rows; this will multiply subject rows (not safe for preserving subject-level metrics unless you re-aggregate enrollments back to SubjectID). | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as classes_with_room_and_building, class_schedule_weekday_flags, student_enrollments_with_status, faculty_teaching_load (if it is by class or instructor) without aggregation, because those joins will duplicate SubjectID rows and thus multiply any subject-level measures. Instead aggregate those one-to-many sources to SubjectID (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT ClassID) BY SubjectID) before joining. | When composing metrics: compute subject-level metrics on this view (or using its SubjectID DISTINCT counts), and compute multi-row aggregates from related one-to-many sources at their own grain, then join on SubjectID (or DepartmentID/CategoryID) only after reducing to the target grain to avoid double-counting. | Joins on CategoryID or DepartmentID are safe for dimension lookups that are one-row-per-category or one-row-per-department (e.g., join to a categories dimension on CategoryID) because Categories is the source of CategoryDescription and DepartmentID here; however, joining to many-subject children via CategoryID/DepartmentID will expand rows and require re-aggregation.

views.description: One row per Subject including its Category and the Category's Department. Useful when analyzing subjects by department or category-level aggregations. | Use for: Group subjects by department; Find all subjects in a category; Join to Classes to get course offerings with department context

views.name: faculty_teaching_load
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Faculty_Classes.StaffID,
  COUNT(Faculty_Classes.ClassID) AS classes_taught,
  SUM(Classes.Credits) AS total_credits_taught
FROM Faculty_Classes
LEFT JOIN Classes ON Faculty_Classes.ClassID = Classes.ClassID
GROUP BY Faculty_Classes.StaffID

params.description: Per-faculty aggregated teaching load: number of classes taught and sum of credits taught, at one row per StaffID.
params.when_to_use: Report total number of classes taught by a faculty member over the underlying Faculty_Classes rows. | Report total credits taught by a faculty member (sum of Credits from Classes for each ClassID they are linked to). | As a building block for per-faculty KPIs (e.g., productivity, workload) when you need one-row-per-staff aggregates to join to faculty dimensions or profiles. | Compose into further aggregations (e.g., department totals) by summing these measures across StaffID, or join to faculty detail for labeling.
params.output_schema: StaffID: unique identifier for a faculty/staff person — derived from Faculty_Classes.StaffID (GROUP BY key). | classes_taught: integer count of distinct Faculty_Classes.ClassID rows associated with the StaffID — derived from COUNT(Faculty_Classes.ClassID) in the view's aggregation. | total_credits_taught: numeric sum of Classes.Credits for ClassID values associated with the StaffID — derived from SUM(Classes.Credits) where Classes is LEFT JOINed on Faculty_Classes.ClassID = Classes.ClassID.
params.metric: classes_taught = COUNT(Faculty_Classes.ClassID)  -- aggregate count of ClassID rows per StaffID from Faculty_Classes | total_credits_taught = SUM(Classes.Credits)  -- aggregate sum of Credits from Classes for the ClassIDs joined to Faculty_Classes
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to faculty_full_profile on faculty_teaching_load.StaffID = faculty_full_profile.StaffID — safe because faculty_teaching_load is one row per StaffID, and faculty_full_profile is expected to be one-row-per-StaffID (JOIN view name implies enrichment), so measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to top_faculty_by_proficiency_rank on StaffID — safe when that view provides a single rank row per StaffID (it is a RANK sibling), preserving one-row-per-StaffID semantics. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: aggregate to department level by SUM(classes_taught) and SUM(total_credits_taught) after joining to subject_category_with_department or faculty_subject_proficiency ONLY if you join via StaffID (or after mapping StaffID→department) and ensure the join target is one-row-per-StaffID; prefer: first join faculty_teaching_load to a faculty-dimension (one row per StaffID) and then roll up by department to avoid duplication. | do NOT join without re-aggregation to one-to-many tables/views such as student_enrollments_with_status (JOIN) or classes_with_room_and_building (JOIN) directly on ClassID or StaffID if those targets are one-to-many relative to StaffID, because those joins can duplicate faculty_teaching_load rows and multiply its measures. Instead: either |   - join faculty_teaching_load to a one-row-per-StaffID dimension/view (e.g., faculty_full_profile) and then join that dimension to many-sided tables, or |   - re-aggregate after the join: e.g., SELECT StaffID, SUM(classes_taught) ... FROM (faculty_teaching_load JOIN classes_with_room_and_building ...) GROUP BY StaffID. | Examples of unsafe joins (will multiply measures unless re-aggregated): |   - joining faculty_teaching_load directly to student_enrollments_with_status on ClassID or StaffID when student_enrollments_with_status has many students per class/staff (one-to-many) — this will duplicate classes_taught and total_credits_taught per matching enrollment row. |   - joining faculty_teaching_load to class_schedule_weekday_flags or classes_with_room_and_building if those sibling views are one-to-many per ClassID (e.g., multiple schedule rows per class or multiple room assignments) without first collapsing them to one row per ClassID or StaffID. | Guiding principle: treat faculty_teaching_load as a facts-at-StaffID-level aggregate (one row per StaffID). It can be safely joined to other one-row-per-StaffID objects without re-aggregation; for joining to any one-to-many dimension from StaffID, either pre-aggregate the many-side, join to a faculty dimension, or re-aggregate the result to restore one-row-per-StaffID before consuming the measures.

views.description: Counts of classes taught per faculty member and total credits taught. Useful for workload and distribution analyses. Grain: one row per StaffID (faculty). | Use for: Who teaches the most classes or credits; Compare teaching load across faculty; Identify faculty with no class assignments (outer join with Faculty)

views.name: students_with_major_and_gpa
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Students.StudentID,
  Students.StudFirstName,
  Students.StudLastName,
  Students.StudStreetAddress,
  Students.StudCity,
  Students.StudState,
  Students.StudZipCode,
  Students.StudAreaCode,
  Students.StudPhoneNumber,
  Students.StudGPA,
  Students.StudMajor,
  Majors.Major AS Major
FROM Students
LEFT JOIN Majors ON Students.StudMajor = Majors.MajorID

params.description: Provides one row per student with that student's contact details, declared major id, major name (if any), and current GPA.
params.when_to_use: List students with their major name and GPA for directory, reporting, or downstream joins that need one row per student. | Filter or group by student attributes (city, state, major) and report counts or aggregates at the student level (e.g., count of students by major). | As a normalized building block to join student-level information into higher-level analyses (courses, enrollments, faculty assignments) while preserving one-row-per-student semantics.
params.output_schema: StudentID: unique identifier for the student — derived from Students.StudentID | StudFirstName: student's first name — derived from Students.StudFirstName | StudLastName: student's last name — derived from Students.StudLastName | StudStreetAddress: student's street address — derived from Students.StudStreetAddress | StudCity: student's city — derived from Students.StudCity | StudState: student's state — derived from Students.StudState | StudZipCode: student's ZIP/postal code — derived from Students.StudZipCode | StudAreaCode: student's phone area code — derived from Students.StudAreaCode | StudPhoneNumber: student's phone number — derived from Students.StudPhoneNumber | StudGPA: student's grade point average (as stored) — derived from Students.StudGPA | StudMajor: foreign key referencing major id on Students — derived from Students.StudMajor | Major: human-readable major name — derived from Majors.Major (left-joined via Students.StudMajor = Majors.MajorID)
params.grounded_columns: Students.StudentID | Students.StudFirstName | Students.StudLastName | Students.StudStreetAddress | Students.StudCity | Students.StudState | Students.StudZipCode | Students.StudAreaCode | Students.StudPhoneNumber | Students.StudGPA | Students.StudMajor | Majors.MajorID | Majors.Major
params.metric: StudGPA = Students.StudGPA (direct stored value; not an aggregate in this view)
params.composition: Safe: join to dimensional/lookups on StudentID (for example student_enrollments_with_status on StudentID) — this view is one-row-per-StudentID, so joining by StudentID will not duplicate the student's row as long as the other side is many-per-student and the query accounts for that multiplicity (e.g., to list enrollments) or the other side is one-row-per-student. | Safe: join to Majors-equivalent lookup tables by StudMajor/MajorID (this view already left-joins Majors; an additional join to other major-level metadata keyed by MajorID is safe because Majors is a one-row-per-major dimension). | Do NOT naively join to one-to-many tables/views (for example class_schedule_weekday_flags, student_enrollments_with_status, faculty_teaching_load, classes_with_room_and_building) without handling multiplicity — those joins will multiply student rows and thus duplicate per-student measures like StudGPA. If you need aggregate measures after joining to a one-to-many table, first aggregate the many-side (e.g., count/enrollments per StudentID) or perform a GROUP BY StudentID to re-collapse to one row per student. | If composing with sibling AGG/RANK views (faculty_subject_proficiency, faculty_teaching_load, top_faculty_by_proficiency_rank), join only on appropriate keys (e.g., FacultyID) and ensure keys do not cause many-to-many duplication. This view contains no FacultyID, so joining to faculty* views requires an intermediate relation (enrollments/courses) and careful aggregation to avoid duplication. | Guidance for planners: treat this view as normalized at the grain StudentID. Any join on StudentID to a dimension that is one-row-per-student is cardinality-safe. Any join to tables keyed at a lower grain (multiple rows per StudentID) requires pre-aggregation or explicit grouping to preserve correct student-level metrics.

views.description: Student dimension projection with major text and a normalized GPA flag indicating low/high (derived continuous); keep raw StudGPA and MajorID for joins. Useful for student cohort selection by GPA or major. | Use for: Select students by major or GPA; Join students to enrollments and classes for performance analysis; Compute counts or averages of GPA by major

views.name: top_faculty_by_proficiency_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  StaffID,
  SubjectID,
  ProficiencyRating,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY SubjectID ORDER BY ProficiencyRating DESC) AS prof_rank
FROM Faculty_Subjects

params.description: For each faculty-staff and subject pair, ranks faculty by their proficiency rating within that subject (highest rating = rank 1).
params.when_to_use: Find top-ranked faculty for a specific subject (e.g., who is rank 1 for Mathematics). | Filter faculty by proficiency rank within a subject (e.g., keep only prof_rank <= 3 for 'top 3' instructors per subject). | Compose with other views to report additional faculty or subject attributes for a given proficiency rank (e.g., join to faculty_full_profile to show contact info for top-ranked faculty). | Aggregate counts of how many staff occupy each prof_rank per subject (when this view is used as the grain of staff×subject). | Create leaderboards by subject without re-computing ranking logic.
params.output_schema: StaffID: identifier of the staff member involved in the faculty-subject assignment; derived directly from Faculty_Subjects.StaffID. | SubjectID: identifier of the subject/course area for which proficiency is recorded; derived directly from Faculty_Subjects.SubjectID. | ProficiencyRating: numeric rating indicating the faculty member's proficiency for that SubjectID; derived directly from Faculty_Subjects.ProficiencyRating. | prof_rank: integer rank within each SubjectID computed by RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY SubjectID ORDER BY ProficiencyRating DESC); higher ProficiencyRating receives a smaller (better) rank. Ties receive the same rank and cause gaps (standard SQL RANK behavior).
params.metric: prof_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY Faculty_Subjects.SubjectID ORDER BY Faculty_Subjects.ProficiencyRating DESC) | ProficiencyRating = Faculty_Subjects.ProficiencyRating (base numeric value, not aggregated)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to faculty_full_profile on StaffID — safe because this view is one-row-per (StaffID, SubjectID) so joining to a one-row-per-StaffID dimension (faculty_full_profile) will not duplicate this view's measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to subject_category_with_department on SubjectID — safe because subject_category_with_department is a subject-level descriptor (one-row-per-SubjectID) so it will not multiply rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to students_with_major_and_gpa only when keyed by StaffID-derived advisor relationship if that other view is one-row-per-StaffID; verify that the sibling view is one-row-per-StaffID before joining to avoid duplication. | do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many child tables/views (for example: class_schedule_weekday_flags, classes_with_room_and_building, student_enrollments_with_status) on SubjectID or StaffID without aggregation, because those joins will multiply the rows per (StaffID, SubjectID) and thus duplicate/proliferate prof_rank and ProficiencyRating values. If you need aggregated results after such a join, first aggregate the child table to the same (StaffID, SubjectID) grain (e.g., count of classes, total enrollment) then join. | do NOT join to faculty_teaching_load (an AGG sibling) unless you understand its grain. If faculty_teaching_load is one-row-per-StaffID, joining on StaffID is safe; if it is one-row-per-StaffID-and-Term or otherwise multi-row per StaffID, aggregate it to one row per StaffID (or per StaffID and SubjectID if appropriate) before joining to avoid duplicating this view's rows. | When composing metrics that sum or average values from this view (e.g., count of top-ranked staff per subject), treat prof_rank as an attribute (dimension), not as a measure to be summed. To produce measures like 'number of rank1 staff per subject', aggregate counts after grouping by SubjectID and filtering prof_rank = 1. | If you need to compute derived measures that combine this view with other multi-row datasets, use explicit aggregation at the composition step (e.g., derive per-subject averages by joining and then GROUP BY SubjectID), ensuring you group at the intended grain to avoid unintended multiplicative effects.

views.description: Per-subject ranking of faculty by ProficiencyRating exposing subject-level rank. Useful as a reusable top-K building block (filter WHERE prof_rank <= K downstream). | Use for: Get top N faculty per subject by proficiency; Identify faculty who are highest-rated for a subject

views.name: completed_student_class_instances
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Student_Schedules.StudentID AS StudentID,
  Student_Schedules.ClassID AS ClassID,
  Student_Schedules.ClassStatus AS ClassStatus,
  Student_Schedules.Grade AS Grade
FROM Student_Schedules
WHERE Student_Schedules.ClassStatus IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per student-class enrollment instance that has been completed (status known). Exposes raw grade and class linkage for downstream filtering and ranking.

views.name: class_with_subject_and_room
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.ClassID,
  c.SubjectID,
  c.ClassRoomID,
  c.StartDate,
  c.StartTime,
  c.Duration
FROM Classes c
JOIN Subjects s ON c.SubjectID = s.SubjectID
JOIN Class_Rooms r ON c.ClassRoomID = r.ClassRoomID
JOIN subject_category_with_department sc ON s.SubjectID = sc.SubjectID
views.description: Class-level metadata joined to its subject and classroom; keeps class scheduling and subject/category linkage so queries can restrict by subject/category and access class times/locations.

views.name: subject_with_category
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Subjects.SubjectID AS SubjectID,
  Subjects.CategoryID AS CategoryID,
  Subjects.SubjectCode AS SubjectCode,
  Subjects.SubjectName AS SubjectName,
  Categories.CategoryDescription AS CategoryDescription
FROM Subjects
LEFT JOIN Categories ON Subjects.CategoryID = Categories.CategoryID
views.description: Subjects annotated with their category description and category id. Useful to filter subjects by human-readable category names (e.g., English) or to group/aggregate by category.
